collection.name: fan-out-documents
collection.description: Per-document processing endpoints for the fan-out (TaskType 21) scenarios. The default route succeeds; document ids starting with DOC-FAIL fail deterministically so the partial-failure leg is exercised without timing games, and ids starting with DOC-SLOW are routed by the mapping to a DELAYED route so item/batch timeouts and the concurrency ceiling can be exercised at all. NOTE — MockLab matches routes by PREFIX: any path beginning with a registered route is answered by that mock. The slow route therefore must NOT be a suffix-extension of the fast one (a route like 'documents/process-slow' is permanently unreachable behind 'documents/process'), which is why it lives under a sibling segment instead.

mocks.description: Processes one document. The fan-out mapping's ItemInputHandler appends ?documentId=<FanOutItem.ItemKey> to this route, which is how each parallel item is told which document it owns — an HttpTask's URL lives on the cloned task, not on the branch body, so the zero-script path could not do this.

Deliberate straggler, selected by the mappings for DOC-SLOW* ids. delayMs is a MOCK-level field — no seed file in this directory has a delay on a rule, and rule objects carry only conditionField/conditionOperator/conditionValue/statusCode/responseBody/contentType/priority/responseHeaders — so a delayed response has to be its own mock. WHY THIS ROUTE IS UNDER 'slow-documents' AND NOT 'documents/process-slow': MockLab matches by PREFIX. While this mock lived at 'api/fan-out/documents/process-slow' every request to it was answered by the 'api/fan-out/documents/process' mock registered above (proven: 'documents/process-XYZQQ' also returns that mock's body), so it was UNREACHABLE and the delay never applied — the straggler answered in 13-46ms and silently made every timeout and concurrency assertion vacuous. Verify after any change to this file that the route returns THIS body (pages 120, slow true) and takes >= 1.4s; 'pages: 3' means the fast mock is still answering. Also note MockLab persists mocks in a container-local DB and skips collections whose name already exists, so a plain 'docker restart' does not re-seed — the container must be recreated (docker compose up -d --force-recreate mocklab).
